What is the atomic number of Flerovium?
Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.
What is the atomic number of Yttrium?
Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.
In what year did Niels Bohr die?
Niels Bohr: Although the Bohr model has been supplanted by other models, its underlying principles remain valid.
In what year was Fluorine discovered?
Fluorine is a chemical element; it has symbol F and atomic number 9.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-15 was one of the first successful jet fighters to incorporate swept wings to perform near Mach 1.
In which country is Mil Mi-8?
Mil Mi-8: Burkina Faso. The Mi-8 is the world's most-produced helicopter, with over 17,000 units used by over 50 countries.
Who is credited with discovering Technetium?
Technetium: Emilio G. Segrè. Technetium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tc and atomic number 43.
Who is credited with discovering Cell theory?
Who is credited with discovering Hydrazine?
Hydrazine: Hermann Emil Fischer. Hydrazine is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula N2H4.
Sharing the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces, who became the first Muslim scientist to win a Nobel?
Abdus Salam (29 January 1926 - 21 November 1996) was a Pakistani theoretical physicist and Nobel laureate.
This exaggerated immune reaction causes the body to mistake a harmless substance for a threat, triggering symptoms from a runny nose to a full anaphylactic reaction — what is it?
Allergy is an exaggerated immune response where the body mistakenly identifies an ordinarily harmless allergen as a threat.
These eusocial insects evolved from vespoid wasps back in the Cretaceous, and you can spot one by its elbowed antennae and pinched, node-like waist. Which creature is it?
Ant are eusocial insects of the family Formicidae and, along with the related wasps and bees, belong to the order Hymenoptera.
With atomic number 85 and symbol At, this is the rarest naturally occurring element in Earth's crust, forming only as a decay product of heavier elements — name it?
Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
A civil-engineering graduate who first reshaped his father's firm toward real estate, this Frenchman now chairs the world's largest luxury goods company — who is he?
Bernard Arnault (born 5 March 1949) is a French businessman.
Native to South American tropical forests, this thorny ornamental vine, bush, or tree produces large colorful bracts surrounding three small waxy flowers — what is this plant genus?
Bougainvillea (US also BOH-) is a genus of thorny ornamental vines, bushes, and trees belonging to the family Nyctaginaceae.
Originating from the now-discredited caloric theory of heat, this unit of energy is defined as the amount of heat needed to raise one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius — name the unit?
Calorie is a unit of energy that originated from the caloric theory of heat.
This class of ribbon-like parasitic flatworms sheds egg-packed body segments called proglottids into the environment to infect new hosts — what is this class called (scientific name)?
Cestoda is a class of parasitic worms in the flatworm phylum (Platyhelminthes).
Once home to a bacterium behind a common cause of diarrhea before its 2016 reclassification, this genus of soil-dwelling bacteria also causes botulism — which genus?
Clostridium is a genus of anaerobic, Gram-positive bacteria.
Released on a daily cycle and spiking when you're stressed, this glucocorticoid raises blood sugar through gluconeogenesis and even tamps down the immune system — what stress hormone is it?
Cortisol is a steroid hormone in the glucocorticoid class of hormones and a stress hormone.
Marked by a telltale skin rash plus progressive muscle weakness, this systemic autoimmune condition can also bring fever, weight loss and light sensitivity — which disease?
Dermatomyositis (DM) is a group of sytemic autoimmune inflammatory diseases primarily affecting the skin and skeletal muscles.
Most of the 68 species sharing this name live in Eurasia and Africa, with only two found in North America — and "true" ones are merely a subfamily; what bird is it?
Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae.
This American investor and podcaster coined the phrase 'intellectual dark web' and proposed a physics framework called 'Geometric Unity' — who is he?
Eric Weinstein (born October 26, 1965) is an American investor and podcast host.

Native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, this fig species carries deep religious significance across four faiths that originated there, including reverence from Hindu and Jain ascetics — what species is it?
Ficus religiosa is a species of fig native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina that belongs to Moraceae, the fig or mulberry family.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this lizard lacks eyelids — instead its eyeballs are covered by a transparent membrane called a brille. What is it?
Gecko are small, mostly carnivorous lizards that have a wide distribution, found on every continent except Antarctica.
One of only two wild camelid species native to South America, this llama relative lives at lower elevations than its cousin, the vicuña — what is it called?
Guanaco (gwah-; Lama guanicoe) is a camelid native to South America, closely related to the domesticated llama.
Never approved by any drug regulator, this THC-like compound made by hydrogenating cannabis isomers has been sold in head-shop vaporizers since the early 2020s — what is it?
Hexahydrocannabinol (HHC) is a phytocannabinoid that has been reported as a minor component of Cannabis oleoresin.

Worldwide, too little dietary iodine is the leading cause of this endocrine condition, in which a sluggish thyroid leaves people cold-intolerant, exhausted, constipated, and prone to weight gain — what is it?
Hypothyroidism is an endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones.
A Scottish surgeon who corrected clubfoot and squints, he's also dubbed by some the 'Father of Modern Hypnotism' — pioneering both hypnotic and chemical anaesthesia. Who was this gentleman scientist?
James Braid (surgeon) (19 June 1795 - 25 March 1860) was a Scottish surgeon, natural philosopher, and "gentleman scientist".
One species of this succulent plant genus, native mainly to Madagascar, became one of the first plants ever sent into space aboard a Soviet space station in 1979 — what genus is it?
Kalanchoe (also called "kalanche" or "kalancho"), is a genus of about 125 species of tropical, succulent plants in the stonecrop family Crassulaceae, mainly native to Madagascar and tropical Africa.

Spread by the bite of sandflies and caused by a genus of protozoal parasites, this tropical disease can present as skin ulcers, disfiguring mucosal damage, or a more dangerous internal form. Name the disease?
Leishmaniasis is a wide array of clinical manifestations caused by protozoal parasites of the Trypanosomatida genus Leishmania.
This evergreen tree, native to the cooler hills of south-central China, is grown commercially for its orange fruit and is sometimes called the Japanese medlar. What is it?
Loquat (Eriobotrya japonica) is a large evergreen shrub or tree grown commercially for its orange coloured fruits.
Following fieldwork with the Omaha people and in Papua New Guinea and Bali, this anthropologist explored gender roles in her 1935 book Sex and Temperament in Three Primitive Societies — who is she?
Margaret Mead (December 16, 1901 - November 15, 1978) was an American cultural anthropologist, author and speaker, who appeared frequently in the mass media during the mid-twentieth century.
Despite little formal education, this self-made English scientist established the concept of the electromagnetic field and uncovered the principles behind electromagnetic induction — who is he?
Michael Faraday (22 September 1791 - 25 August 1867) was an English chemist and physicist who contributed vastly to the study of electrochemistry and electromagnetism.
This group of more than 30 rare neuromuscular disorders causes skeletal tissue to progressively weaken and break down, differing in which body parts are hit first and how fast — what's it called?
Muscular dystrophy (MD) is a genetically and clinically heterogeneous group of rare neuromuscular diseases that cause progressive weakness and breakdown of skeletal muscles over time.
This raised region of tissue on the breast, surrounded by the darker-colored areola, is where milk exits the body through the lactiferous ducts during breastfeeding — name this body part?
Nipple is a raised region of tissue on the surface of the breast from which, in lactating females, milk from the mammary gland leaves the body through the lactiferous ducts to nurse an infant.
Usually caused by bacteria and sometimes requiring amputation in severe cases, this infectious inflammation of bone can be acute or chronic — which condition?
Osteomyelitis (OM) is the infectious inflammation of bone. It may be acute or chronic and can be classified as hematogenous or non-hematogenous.
Recognized by a long beak and an enormous throat pouch used to drain water from scooped-up prey before swallowing, these large water birds come in eight living species worldwide — which birds?
Pelican (genus Pelecanus) are a genus of large water birds that make up the family Pelecanidae.
What small, tailless, round-bodied mountain mammal — a close relative of the rabbit with short rounded ears — includes a large-eared Himalayan species that lives above 6,000 meters?
Pika is a small, mountain-dwelling mammal native to Asia and North America.
Lacking any real scientific definition, this British term for a large swimming crustacean has become almost interchangeable with 'shrimp' — what is it?
Prawn is a common name for small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs (members of the order of decapods), some of which are edible.
A zoonotic virus that triggers violent movements, a dread of water, and almost certain death once symptoms set in — usually one to three months after exposure. What is this disease?
Rabies is a zoonotic viral disease that causes acute and severe encephalitis in humans and other mammals.
This British economist won the 1991 Nobel Memorial Prize and warned that the field was "suicidal" to become a hard science of choice while ignoring society, history, and culture — who was he?
Ronald Coase (29 December 1910 - 2 September 2013) was a British economist and author.
Which leathery-skinned marine echinoderm, of which about 1,786 species are known worldwide, plays a vital ecological role on the sea floor by breaking down detritus as a scavenger?
Sea cucumber are echinoderms from the class Holothuroidea.
Which urban model uses digital technology and data from citizens, buildings, and cameras to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion?
Smart city is an urban model that leverages technology, human capital, and governance to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion, which are considered goals for cities of the future.
Born in 1955, this former physician left medicine to pursue UFO research, founding an organization dedicated to studying extraterrestrial intelligence — who is he?
Steven M. Greer (born 1955) is an American ufologist and a retired physician.

This chalcogen element, chemically similar to selenium and sulfur, is far more abundant in the universe than on Earth because its hydride escaped into space during our planet's formation — which element?
Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
Dolphins, porpoises, beaked whales and sperm whales all belong to this cetacean group that diverged from baleen whales around 34 million years ago — what's the collective name?

Toothed whale (also called odontocetes, systematic name Odontoceti) are a parvorder of cetaceans that includes dolphins, porpoises, and all other whales with teeth, such as beaked whales and the sperm whales.
As head of the WWII Office of Scientific Research and Development, this MIT engineer steered nearly all American military R&D, including radar and the early Manhattan Project — who was he?
Vannevar Bush (van-; March 11, 1890 - June 28, 1974) was an American engineer, inventor and science administrator, who during World War II headed the U.S.

This bird family, which also includes piculets, wrynecks, and sapsuckers, is absent from Australia and Madagascar, though one desert-dwelling member has adapted to drill into cacti — what family of birds is it?
Woodpecker are part of the bird family Picidae, which also includes the piculets, wrynecks, and sapsuckers.
The simplest and smallest ketone, this colorless, pungent, highly flammable liquid mixes freely with water and lurks in nail polish remover and paint thinner — what is it?
Working at Baghdad's House of Wisdom around 820, this Islamic Golden Age scholar wrote a treatise whose Arabic title, Al-Jabr, gave us the very word "algebra." Who was he?
This Indian economist and philosopher won the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his work on welfare economics, and later received India's highest civilian honor — who is he?
Amartya Sen: Indian economist and Nobel laureate (born 1933)
Named by paleontologist Barnum Brown in 1908, this armored dinosaur is considered the archetypal member of its group despite no complete skeleton ever being found — which genus?
Ankylosaurus: Ankylosaurid dinosaur genus from the Late Cretaceous Period.
Native to the Philippines and spread by Austronesian voyagers as early as 1500 BCE, this palm's fruit is chewed with slaked lime and betel leaves for its stimulant effects — which species?
Areca catechu: Species of palm. It was carried widely through the tropics by the Austronesian migrations and trade since at least 1500 BCE due to its use in betel nut chewing.

Despite its name being something of a misnomer, this herding dog breed was developed in California and takes its name from imported collies that arrived alongside sheep from Down Under — what breed is it?
Australian Shepherd: American breed of dog. The Australian Shepherd, also known as the Aussie, is a breed of herding dog from the United States.
This inflammatory condition causes recurring, painful mouth sores along with eye inflammation and arthritis, and is diagnosed after at least three sore outbreaks in a year — which condition?
Behçet's disease: Inflammatory disorder. Behçet's disease or Behçet's syndrome (BD; sometimes written Behcet) is a type of inflammatory disorder which affects multiple parts of the body.
Rich in vitamin C and polyphenols, this deciduous shrub's glossy dark berries are cooked into jams and syrups or fermented into cassis — what is it?
Blackcurrant: Species of flowering plant in the gooseberry family Grossulariaceae.

This infraorder of decapod crustaceans tucks a stubby tail-like abdomen under a hard shell and ends its front pair of legs in pincers — over 1.5 million tonnes of them are eaten by humans yearly. What group is it?
Brachyura: Crustacean. The true crabs are the largest of the crab decapod groups with carcinised body forms.
A cole crop related to broccoli, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts, the heaviest recorded head of this leafy vegetable weighed nearly 138 pounds — what is it?
Cabbage: Leafy vegetable in the flowering plant family Brassicaceae.
This infraorder of decapod crustaceans is the true taxonomic home of what everyone actually calls a shrimp, found in fresh and salt water worldwide — what is it?
The largest part of the brain, this structure houses the cerebral cortex plus the hippocampus and basal ganglia, and works with the cerebellum to control every voluntary action. What is it?
Cerebrum: Large part of the brain containing the cerebral cortex.
Selected from over 11,000 applicants for NASA's Teacher in Space Project, this Concord, New Hampshire educator died aboard the Challenger in 1986 — who was she?
Christa McAuliffe: American teacher and astronaut (1948–1986)
Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy, this opiate is a prodrug of morphine often paired with paracetamol to treat mild pain, coughs, and even diarrhea — what is it?
Codeine: Opiate and prodrug of morphine used to treat pain. It usually starts working after half an hour, with maximum effect at two hours.
Caused by a fungus that forms galls on maize plants, this disease produces an edible delicacy in Mexico known as huitlacoche, often stuffed into quesadillas — which condition?
Corn smut: Fungal plant disease on maize and teosinte.
Also called Bermuda grass, this hardy warm-climate turf species is ironically not native to the island of the same name — which plant, by its scientific name?
Cynodon dactylon: Species of grass. Cynodon dactylon, commonly known as Bermuda grass or as couch grass in Australia and New Zealand, is a grass found worldwide in warm and tropical climates.
This central nervous system stimulant is the 'right-handed' mirror-image form of a well-known molecule, prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy and sometimes given as an inactive prodrug — what is it?
Dextroamphetamine: CNS stimulant and isomer of amphetamine.
A broad-spectrum member of the tetracycline class, this antibiotic treats everything from acne and chlamydia to Lyme disease and cholera — though it'll make you sunburn more easily. Which drug?
Doxycycline: Tetracycline-class antibiotic. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
Despite its name, this South American freshwater fish is actually a knifefish, not a true eel, and produces powerful discharges using specialized tissue — which species?
Electrophorus electricus: South American electric fish. It is considered as a freshwater teleost which contains an electrogenic tissue that produces electric discharges.
This flowering shrub in the family Erythroxylaceae is one of only two species whose leaves are cultivated to produce a notorious stimulant — which plant is it?
Erythroxylum coca: Species of flowering plant.
Sporting an orange-red breast rimmed in grey and brown upperparts, this small insect-eating songbird ranges from Western Siberia to North Africa — which bird?
European robin: Species of bird. It is found across Europe, as far east as Western Siberia, and as far south as North Africa.

Boldly patterned in black and yellow to warn predators of its toxicity, this European amphibian can live for more than 50 years and is now vulnerable due to an introduced fungal disease — what species is it?
Fire salamander: Species of amphibian. The fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) is a common species of salamander found in Europe.
Traditionally pounded from cassava, plantains, and cocoyam, this West African staple gets a shoutout in Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart — what dish is it?
Fufu: Dough-like food in African cuisine.
The largest of its family, this mostly solitary mammal uses long foreclaws to dig into nests and a sticky tongue to slurp up ants and termites — what animal is it?
Giant anteater: Species of mammal. The giant anteater (Myrmecophaga tridactyla) is an insectivorous mammal native to Central and South America.
One of China's 'Four Great Domestic Fish,' this herbivorous freshwater species was later introduced to Europe and the US to control aquatic weeds — which fish?
Grass carp: Species of fish. This Asian carp is the only species of the genus Ctenopharyngodon.

This prehensile, multi-fingered body part sits at the end of primates' forelimbs — koalas famously have two opposable thumbs on each one, while raccoons are often said to have them despite lacking true opposable thumbs. What is it?
Hand: Extremity at the end of an arm or forelimb.

First synthesized in 1940 by chemist Roger Adams via hydrogenation of THC isomers, this psychoactive cannabis-derived compound is sold in vaporizers despite never being drug-approved — which compound?
Lightest and most abundant element in the universe, it makes up about 75% of all normal matter and fuels the stars — colorless, odorless, and highly combustible. What element is it?
Hydrogen: Chemical element with atomic number 1 (H)
Equal to one-twelfth of a foot and derived from the Roman word for 'twelfth,' this unit of length has been pegged to exactly 25.4 millimeters since the mid-20th century — what is it?
Inch: Unit of length. The inch (symbol: in or ″) is a unit of length in the British Imperial and the United States customary systems of measurement.

The New York Times once called him "the nation's most influential evangelical leader," yet he was never an ordained minister — instead this psychologist founded Focus on the Family and led it from 1977 to 2010. Who was he?
James Dobson: American evangelical Christian psychologist and author (1936–2025)
This Hungarian-American polymath helped build the mathematical framework of quantum physics and codified ideas from game theory to cellular automata — who was he?
John von Neumann: Hungarian and American mathematician and physicist (1903–1957)
A German mechanical engineer turned economist, he founded a famous annual gathering of global leaders in 1971 and chaired it until stepping down in 2025. Who is he?
Klaus Schwab: Founder of the World Economic Forum (born 1938)

An Atlanta factory superintendent with a Cornell engineering degree, he was wrongly convicted of murdering a young employee, then kidnapped from prison and lynched — a case that became a focus of antisemitism. Who was he?
The third wide-body airliner to enter service after the 747 and DC-10, this trijet used an S-duct to route its third engine through the tail — which aircraft?

Lockheed L-1011 TriStar: American wide-body trijet airliner. The Lockheed L-1011 TriStar (pronounced "El-ten-eleven") is an American medium-to-long-range, wide-body trijet airliner built by the Lockheed Corporation.

Founder of the Kerala school, this Indian mathematician was the first to use infinite series to approximate trigonometric functions — a 'decisive step' toward the limit-passage to infinity; who is he?
Madhava of Sangamagrama: Indian mathematician and astronomer (1340–1425)

Captured by Einstein's famous equation E=mc², this principle shows that a tiny amount of one physical quantity converts into an enormous amount of another thanks to the speed of light being squared — what is this relationship called?
Mass–energy equivalence: Physics concept expressed as E = mc².
In medicine, this term describes a disease spreading from a primary site to a secondary one — most often used for a cancer seeding new tumors elsewhere in the body — what is it?
Metastasis: Spreading of a disease inside a body. The newly pathological sites, then, are metastases (mets).
This Israeli-American physician turned billionaire donor owns the Las Vegas Review-Journal and Dallas Mavericks, and was one of Donald Trump's largest financial backers — who is she?

Miriam Adelson: Israeli-American physician, billionaire, and conservative donor. Miriam Adelson (née Farbstein; born October 10, 1945) is an Israeli-American physician, businesswoman, philanthropist, and conservative political donor.
Sold under the brand name Bactroban, this topical antibiotic treats impetigo and clears MRSA from the nose — what is it?
Derived from the Greek word for kidney, this medical specialty covers kidney function, disease, and treatments ranging from diet changes to dialysis and transplantation — which field?
Nephrology: Medical study concerned with the kidneys.
Built from nucleotide units — a sugar, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base — this biomolecule class includes both DNA and RNA. Which class of molecule?
Nucleic acid: Class of large biomolecules essential to all known life.

This vertebrate clade has skeletons made mostly of bone rather than cartilage, and includes both classic 'bony fish' and, cladistically, every land vertebrate descended from lobe-finned ancestors — what is it?
Osteichthyes: Diverse clade of vertebrate animals.
Known as the passion flower, this genus of about 550 species also has ornamental hybrids that have won Royal Horticultural Society awards and varieties used in ayahuasca analogs — name the genus?
Passiflora: Genus of flowering plants in the passion flower family.
What is the process by which immune cells like macrophages and neutrophils engulf pathogens and debris with their plasma membrane, forming an internal compartment called a phagosome?
Phagocytosis: Cell membrane engulfing a large particle.
This self-limiting skin condition begins with a single “herald patch” before smaller scaly spots erupt days later, usually clearing up on its own within three months — which condition?
Pityriasis rosea: Skin disease. It usually lasts less than three months and goes away without treatment.
Used to disinfect skin before and after surgery, this antiseptic can cause kidney problems and high blood sodium if applied to large wounds, and comes as a liquid, ointment, or powder — what is it?
Povidone-iodine: Antiseptic solution. Povidone-iodine (PVP-I), also known as iodopovidone, is an antiseptic used for skin disinfection before and after surgery.

Covering the asymmetric relationship between citizens and the state — including constitutional, administrative, tax, and criminal matters — this branch of the legal system contrasts with the branch governing relationships between individuals — which branch?
Public law: Law governing government actions.
One of the oldest groups of eukaryotic seaweed, this phylum boasts over 7,000 species — mostly marine, though about 5% live in freshwater habitats. What group is it?
Red algae: Division of plant life.

Also called black locust or false acacia, this deciduous legume-family tree is native to just a few small pockets of the United States but has been planted so widely it's now considered invasive elsewhere — which tree?
Robinia pseudoacacia: Species of tree native to North America.
Containing the potent compound salvinorin A, this plant used by Mazatec shamans for spiritual healing sparked a US media panic around 2007 after being shared in online videos — which plant?
Salvia divinorum: Species of plant. The leaves contain the potent compound salvinorin A and can induce a dissociative state and hallucinations.
Ejaculated through the urethra and containing fructose plus enzymes that help sperm survive their journey to fertilize an egg, this bodily fluid is also collected for animal breeding. What is it?
Semen: Reproductive biofluid of male or hermaphroditic animals.

A parasomnia in which wakefulness and deep non-REM sleep occur in different brain regions at once, this condition can produce anything from bathroom trips to attempts at cooking or even driving — what is it?
Sleepwalking: Sleeping phenomenon combined with wakefulness.

Synthesized by Aristotle and taken as fact for two millennia, this superseded theory held that maggots could arise straight from dead flesh, until Louis Pasteur helped discredit it — what was it called?
Spontaneous generation: Theory of life arising from non-living matter.
Born from Russia's PAK FA programme begun in 1999 and carrying the internal name T-50, this twin-engine jet was the first Russian military aircraft built with stealth technology — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-57: Russian stealth multirole fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the brown raptor, this nocturnal bird of prey nests in tree hollows across Europe and is so territorial that evicted youngsters may starve — what is it?
Tawny owl: Stocky medium-sized owl species.

Marked by platelet counts that fall too low — sometimes below 50,000 per microliter and requiring emergency care — this blood disorder is the most common coagulation problem in ICU patients — what is it called?
Thrombocytopenia: Abnormally low levels of platelets in the blood.
This spiral-shaped bacterium, spread mainly through sexual contact and known only to infect humans and baboons, causes syphilis along with yaws and bejel — what is it?
Treponema pallidum: Species of bacterium. T. pallidum can enter the host through mucosal membranes or open lesions in the skin and is primarily spread through sexual contact.
This medical specialty treats the kidneys, bladder and urinary tract, along with the male reproductive organs, covering conditions from infections to kidney stones — which field of medicine?
Urology: Medical specialty on the urinary and reproductive systems. The urinary and reproductive tracts are closely linked, and disorders of one often affect the other.
As DuPont's leader of organic chemistry, this American chemist laid the groundwork for neoprene and is credited with inventing one world-changing synthetic fiber — who was he?
Wallace Carothers: American chemist and inventor (1896–1937)
With atomic number 54, this dense, colorless noble gas was the first to form a stable chemical compound, and now doubles as a general anesthetic and ion-thruster propellant — which element?
Xenon: Chemical element with atomic number 54 (Xe). It is a dense, colorless, odorless noble gas found in Earth's atmosphere in trace amounts.
